theme: Election Day: Strategy spends more on STRC buybacks than bitcoin, ETF outflows hit bitcoin near $77K, the VIX sits near 20 as the Nasdaq-100 enters a correction, Big Tech's unbooked leases top $1 trillion while net cash splits the AI spenders, Drax plans a UK gigawatt campus, SpaceX trades near its IPO price, and Tesla adds Fort Worth.

items.title: Strategy's STRC buybacks as a share of weekly STRC volume
items.picked: Strategy's Monday 8-K said it bought back 2,092,035 STRC shares for $208.2 million last week, more than three times the $65.5 million it spent on 811 BTC. That brings its holdings to 849,327 BTC, per the filing and Cointelegraph.
items.matters: Buying back its own preferred stock supports STRC's price near par, but money spent on buybacks is money that doesn't buy bitcoin. This chart shows how big a share of STRC's trading those buybacks have become.
items.know: In the latest week in the tab, the week of Oct 19 2026, Strategy repurchased 2,068,459 STRC shares for $204.9 million, 27.7% of the shares traded. The high was 29.6% in the week of Oct 5, and the 14 weeks from Jul 20 total $2,043.2 million. The tab doesn't yet include the Oct 26 or Nov 2 8-K weeks, so it is about two weeks stale. The image was redrawn from the tab because the export showed the Total and Source rows as bars.

items.title: US spot bitcoin ETF daily net flows
items.picked: A story trending on X says BlackRock's IBIT had a $405.3 million outflow on Nov 2, its biggest in over four months, with about $399 million leaving US spot bitcoin ETFs overall as bitcoin tested $76,800 on Election Day.
items.matters: ETF flows are the clearest daily read on US institutional demand for bitcoin. A run of large outflows usually lines up with weak prices.
items.know: The tab's latest day is Oct 30 2026, a net outflow of $643.2 million, the largest since $691.7 million on Jun 25. October came to a net outflow of $515.9 million over 22 trading days, the first negative month since June's $4.51 billion. The tab, sourced from Farside, doesn't yet include the Nov 2 outflow.

items.title: Crypto since the Nov 5 2024 US election: bitcoin, ether, Solana and XRP
items.picked: With the midterms underway, stories trending on X have bitcoin traders weighing past post-midterm drops against gains a year later, while bitcoin holds near $77,000.
items.matters: The 2024 election kicked off a big crypto rally, and this chart shows how much of that move each major coin has kept two years on.
items.know: Indexed to Nov 5 2024 = 100, the tab's latest weekly point (Oct 30 2026) has bitcoin at 111.3, ether at 92.5, Solana at 57.7 and XRP at 244.0. Bitcoin peaked at 176.3 in the week of Oct 3 2025 and bottomed at 86.5 on Jun 26 2026. The data is weekly and ends Oct 30, before this week's dip.

items.title: VIX vs S&P 500: ten years of weekly closes
items.picked: US stock futures were mixed on Election Day, and the Nasdaq-100 closed more than 10% below its record on Monday, in a correction, per Reuters. CNBC says a Democratic sweep could hit AI stocks on Wednesday.
items.matters: The VIX is the market's price for S&P 500 volatility over the next 30 days. It tends to rise before events like elections and fall once the results are known.
items.know: On the tab's latest weekly close, Oct 30 2026, the S&P 500 was at 7,580.07, 3.0% below its Oct 9 record weekly close of 7,811.54, and the VIX was 19.42. The VIX closed near 19.4 to 20 in each of the last three weeks, its highest weekly closes since Jun 5 (21.51), but well below the 2026 high of 31.05 on Mar 27. The image was redrawn from the tab with VIX on its own axis, because the export plotted it on the S&P scale.

items.title: Nasdaq: the dot-com run vs the AI run
items.picked: Reuters reports the Nasdaq-100 closed more than 10% below its all-time closing high on Monday, confirming a correction as investors question Big Tech's AI spending. Apple fell premarket on a memory-cost warning.
items.matters: Comparisons to 1999 come back every time AI stocks fall, and this chart lines up both runs by trading days since their start.
items.know: Indexed to 100 at the start, the AI-era Nasdaq (from Nov 30 2022) was at 231.51 on trading day 980, the tab's latest point, down from its high of 240.14 on day 965. At the same point the dot-com run (from Aug 9 1995) was at 258.92, and it didn't peak until day 1,155, at 482.32. The tab samples every five trading days, so this week's moves aren't in it.

items.tab: 22 Big Tech unbooked leases by co
items.title: Signed, not yet on the books: Big Tech's data-center leases
items.picked: A story trending on X says filings show $3.3 trillion of off-balance-sheet AI commitments at Big Tech, led by Alphabet at $1.06 trillion, and investors are pulling back from tech stocks.
items.matters: Leases that are signed but haven't started don't show up as debt yet, but they are fixed future payments for data centers. They will hit the balance sheets as the buildings come online.
items.know: At Sep 30 2026 the tab has $1.02 trillion of leases not yet commenced: Microsoft $364.6B, Meta $355.7B, Amazon $164.9B and Alphabet $130.5B, up from $282B a year earlier. This counts leases only, so it is smaller than the $3.3 trillion figure, which includes other commitments, and Oracle (tab 18: $288B at Aug 31) is excluded. The image was redrawn from the tab because the export's title still said $830B (Jun 2026).

items.title: Hyperscaler net cash: who still has more cash than debt
items.picked: Reuters notes several tech companies have tapped the bond market to fund AI spending, and Amazon reported negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over 12 months, per The Washington Times.
items.matters: Net cash shows how much room each company has to keep spending before it has to borrow more. It has started to separate the AI spenders.
items.know: On the latest balance sheets in the tab (Sep 30 2026, Oracle Aug 31), Alphabet has $139.0B of net cash, SpaceX $52.0B and Microsoft $29.0B. Meta is about even at -$1.3B, while Amazon (-$66.1B) and Oracle (-$88.2B) are in net debt. The tab leaves out operating and finance leases, which would push every figure lower.

items.title: Data center capacity by country: operational vs pipeline
items.picked: Brookfield, Drax and the neocloud Radiant plan a gigawatt-scale AI data center at Drax's North Yorkshire power station, starting with 100 MW by early 2028, per CNBC and The Guardian. Drax shares rose 8%.
items.matters: Power and buildings are the bottleneck for AI compute, and this chart shows how far ahead the US is in both live and planned capacity.
items.know: The tab has the US at 31.97 GW operational with 70.63 GW more in the pipeline, against 5.49 GW operational in China. The UK has 1.76 GW operational and 2.36 GW in the pipeline, so a 1 GW Drax campus would be large for the UK. The source is Cushman & Wakefield's 2026 comparison as analysed in April, so it isn't a live count.

items.title: SpaceX since the IPO: drawdown from peak and 10-day volatility vs Tesla
items.picked: SpaceX fell 6.37% on Friday to $134.72, just below its $135 IPO price, then rose 1.22% to $136.37 on Monday on a report that it is in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile, per The Washington Times and The Motley Fool.
items.matters: Drawdown and volatility show how rough holding SPCX has been since its June IPO, and how much more it swings than Tesla.
items.know: On the tab's latest day, Oct 30 2026, SPCX was 36.27% below its record close, with 10-day realized volatility of 74.43% against Tesla's 43.0%. Its deepest drawdown was 48.78% on Aug 5. The tab ends Oct 30, so it doesn't include Monday's bounce.

items.title: Texas robotaxi registrations: Tesla vs Waymo
items.picked: Tesla opened unsupervised Robotaxi rides in Fort Worth on Nov 2, its seventh unsupervised city and fourth in Texas, with a 143-square-mile geofence, per Not a Tesla App and Fort Worth Report.
items.matters: Registered vehicles are a public, regularly updated read on how fast Tesla is adding cars to its robotaxi fleet compared with Waymo.
items.know: As of Oct 31 2026 the tab has 1,204 Tesla vehicles on the Texas registry (631 Model Y and 573 Cybercab) against 1,259 for Waymo, with Avride at 344 and Zoox at 63. These are registered vehicles, not cars giving rides, and the registry doesn't assign them to cities, so the Fort Worth fleet size isn't known. The image was redrawn from the tab because the export's title still showed the Oct 28 counts.
